Where it began

Adil Rashid was born in Bradford on 17 February 1988, and his brothers Haroon and Amar also became cricketers. Terry Jenner spotted him at 14, and at 17 he was taking six wickets in an innings for the Yorkshire Academy and making a hundred for the county's under-17s.

His first-class debut came in 2006 at Scarborough, standing in for Darren Lehmann, and he marked it by taking six wickets in Warwickshire's second innings to win the match. That summer he also made a hundred and took eight wickets in an innings in a youth Test for England against India. In 2007 the Cricket Writers' Club and the players' union both named him the best young cricketer in the country.

The player

England first picked him in 2009, and his one-day career took off in 2015. Called up against New Zealand, he reached fifty in 37 balls and shared a seventh-wicket stand of 177 with Jos Buttler, a world record in one-day internationals, then took four wickets for good measure.

His Test debut came that October in Abu Dhabi. The first innings was long and wicketless, but in the second he took five for 64 and nearly bowled England to victory. Across 19 Tests between 2015 and 2019 he took 60 wickets at 39.83, with a best of 5 for 49, and made 540 runs with two fifties. He was part of the England sides that won the 50-over World Cup in 2019 and the T20 World Cup in 2022.

What made him special

He had a full set of tricks, the leg-break, the googly, the top-spinner and the slider, to keep batters guessing. That made him a match-winner in the short formats. In 2020 he became the first England spinner to take 150 one-day international wickets, and he went on to become England's leading wicket-taker in T20 internationals.

Test cricket was a tougher nut, and his wickets there cost rather more than in the one-day game. Even so, in India in 2016–17 he took four wickets in an innings four times, in a series where India made 631 and 759 in successive Tests. He was also a better batter than most bowlers, with a first-class best of 180.

Away from the middle

He spent a winter in the Big Bash with South Australia in 2010–11, bowling alongside a young Nathan Lyon, and they won the title together. In 2018 he became an ambassador for a Yorkshire charity that does most of its work in the Punjab, and in 2023 he was made an MBE for services to cricket.

And finally

In 2015 Yorkshire wanted him back from an England match in Ireland so badly that they hired a private jet. He repaid them by taking four wickets in each innings against Hampshire, which is about as good a return on an air fare as any county has had.
